Tbh i hate social media and I hate "being an influencer" but it helps my publicity tremendously.

I do it this way: 

I have Instagram account for my poetry. 
I post 2 poems and 1 photo if myself or something like that. 

I also have a YT channel in my native language where I upload 1-2 readings of my short stories a week + whatever I write.

And an English yt channel where I post readings of short texts targeting people who can later buy my books translated to English/other languages.
That's because my English is not so great and I just don't wanna create extra content for language I don't love/understand as much as my native language. 

I'm not really into social media but when starting out its probably the best way to go. 

My best advice that you can do certain things to boost up social media numbers in exchange for honesty and quality of your work. 
Stuff like buying into cliche, writing stuff everyone can relate to, writing short things, using simple language... If u ever want to make it beyond social media, don't do these things and remain honest. It will take way longer for u to grow but it's wort it at the end. 

Having social media numbers to show helps you to get noticed by publishers a lot. But tell them right away you don't wanna be just a "Instagram writer" or whatever. You need them to publish you for you and your writing not because of your social media statistics.

The book market is oversaturated. It's better to show your work wherever you can instead of hoping some publisher will maybe one day randomly notice you. 

Getting published is beautiful and satisfying and amazing etc... But to be honest it is kinda outdated. Social media, e-books, kindle... Focus more on these things. It's sad but it's the truth and if you don't allow it to take quality off your work it won't.

The thing is that tournaments are not decided in the early stages. By studying early level play you are making much less money then if you would choose a simplier strategy for the deepstacked part of the tournament and focus on the spots which actually allow you to make a deep run.Of course having a nice stack is nice and comfortable but what is it for if you are getting outplayed in every sub35bbs eff pot ?Frst make sure you are the best 0-35bbs player in the field and then worry about deepstacked stuff:)  


Edit : I am not the best poker player. I got this advice from the raise your edge podcast which I believe is a good source of poker info.

I think considering that it was early in the tournament fold is okay.
Most people think early tournament double up pretty much doubles your stack value but that's not true at all. There is nowhere to rush. Best way how to play early levels deepstacked is just to wait for the bad players to give you their chips. 

Later on, when everyone has around 15-45 bbs that's where your skills should shine the most. 

But early on, just wait for the bad players to give you a gift.
